sections.title: 1. Metropolitan Giants & Inland Centers (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Rakhigarhi)
sections.content:
The core urbanism of the Indus Civilisation is defined by its massive metropolitan giants. Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, and Rakhigarhi were primary socio-political hubs, displaying highly standardized city planning, brick ratios, and sanitary engineering.

Harappa & Mohenjo-daro Layouts
  • Standard Grid & Citadel: Both cities featured a raised western Citadel (for public and administrative uses) and a lower eastern residential town. Roads crossed at right angles.
  • Mohenjo-daro Monuments: Key public structures include the Great Bath (sealed with natural bitumen/tar), the Great Granary (with ventilation air ducts), and the Assembly Hall.
  • Harappa Discoveries: Circular brick platforms for threshing grain, parallel rows of granaries outside the citadel, and Cemetery R-37 featuring wooden coffin burials.
Rakhigarhi: The Largest Metropolis

Situated in Haryana's Hisar district along the dry Drishadvati channel, Rakhigarhi has emerged as the largest Harappan site, covering over 350-500 hectares across nine mounds. Recent DNA analysis of skeletal remains from its cemetery has provided critical insights, indicating a lack of major migrations from the West during the Harappan period and pointing to indigenous development of South Asian ancestry.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Harappans construct their granaries near river banks?

masteryZone.q: Why was natural bitumen applied to the Great Bath?
masteryZone.sol: To seal the brickwork and prevent water from leaking or seeping into the surrounding foundations of the Citadel mound.

masteryZone.q: Why are the Rakhigarhi skeletal DNA findings significant?
masteryZone.sol: They suggest that the South Asian ancestral gene pool was formed indigenous to the region, without large migrations from Central Asia during the Harappan era.

masteryZone.q: How did the Harappan street grid system ensure efficient urban traffic?
masteryZone.sol: By planning wide, parallel avenues crossing at right angles, which separated fast-moving cart traffic from narrow residential alleys.

masteryZone.q: How was water supplied to the Great Bath?
masteryZone.sol: Water was drawn from a large, brick-lined well located in an adjacent room and channeled into the bath through an inlet.

masteryZone.q: How did the dual citadel-lower town structure reflect social stratification?
masteryZone.sol: The raised citadel housed elite public buildings, granaries, and administrative offices, while the larger lower town was built for common citizens and artisans.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro
masteryZone.sol: A monumental public water basin made of baked bricks, gypsum mortar, and watertight bitumen. Features changing rooms and an outlet drain, indicating its use for collective ritual purification rather than daily sanitation.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Rakhigarhi Cemetery Excavations
masteryZone.sol: Excavations yielded skeletal remains with intact petrous bones, enabling successful ancient DNA sequencing. Results proved genetic continuity of South Asian ancestry without Steppe migrations during the Mature phase.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Parallel Granaries and Circular Platforms of Harappa
masteryZone.sol: Large storage platforms raised on brick podiums with threshing circles nearby, showing systematic collection, processing, and redistribution of grain by a centralized administrative authority.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Harappan Grid Town Planning
masteryZone.sol: Explain how streets were aligned along cardinal directions (North-South, East-West) to exploit prevailing winds for street cleaning, utilizing standard brick ratios and integrated drainage lines in all sectors.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: The Lost-Wax Bronze Casting
masteryZone.sol: Explain the cire perdue method: modeling in wax, applying clay layers, heating to drain the melted wax, pouring molten bronze, and breaking the mold to reveal solid sculptures like the Dancing Girl.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Archaeological Citadels
masteryZone.sol: Explain that Citadels were fortified raised mounds containing public, ritual, and administrative spaces, functioning as the civic and political heart of the settlement, separated from residential zones.

sections.title: 2. Ports, Trade Outposts & Industrial Suburbs (Lothal, Sutkagendor, Chanhudaro, Kuntasi)
sections.content:
While metropolises handled administrative affairs, trade outposts, ports, and industrial suburbs were the engines of the Indus Valley's complex economy, securing raw materials and managing maritime commerce.

Maritime Ports: Lothal & Sutkagendor
  • Lothal Dockyard: A massive trapezoidal artificial basin built of baked bricks, connected to the Bhogavo River. It served as a tidal dockyard for shipping.
  • Lothal Findings: Joint/double burials, Persian Gulf-type seals, a bead factory, and terracotta ship models indicating direct trade with Mesopotamia.
  • Sutkagendor: Situated on the Dasht River, this western outpost served as a coastal trading port and fortified buffer to manage the overland and sea routes into the Persian Gulf.
Industrial Suburbs: Chanhudaro & Kuntasi

Chanhudaro in Sindh was a pure craft town that completely lacked a fortified citadel. It was famous for shell-working, seal-cutting, and bead-making factories, yielding bronze toy carts and an inkpot. Kuntasi in Gujarat acted as a small port and industrial settlement specializing in bead-making and copper processing.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Harappans establish an outpost at Sutkagendor?

masteryZone.sol: To withstand water pressure and erosion caused by constant tidal inflows and outflows from the Bhogavo River and Gulf.

masteryZone.q: How did Lothal's dockyard operate using tides?
masteryZone.sol: Ships entered the basin during high tides through an inlet channel. A wooden sluice gate was lowered at low tide to trap water and float ships for loading/unloading.

masteryZone.q: How did bead-makers color carnelian stone red?
masteryZone.sol: By heating yellowish-brown raw stones in clay pots over open fires, causing iron oxides in the stone to oxidize into a bright red color.

masteryZone.q: How did Sutkagendor facilitate overland and sea trade?
masteryZone.sol: Its location at the Dasht River mouth allowed it to monitor sea traffic while connecting with inland camel caravan routes passing through Iran.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Lothal Dockyard
masteryZone.sol: A massive trapezoidal brick basin measuring 217m x 37m, connected to a river channel. It is the earliest known artificial dockyard in the world, showcasing advanced understanding of tidal flow, sluice engineering, and maritime shipping.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Bead Manufacture at Chanhudaro
masteryZone.sol: Excavations revealed working floors, furnaces, stone chips, and specialized chert drills. The find proves that bead making was a highly structured, state-sponsored industry with specialized labor producing goods for local use and export.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Sutkagendor Outpost
masteryZone.sol: Located in the arid Makran coast. It features a walled citadel built of massive stone blocks, showing that the Harappans fortified their trade outposts on hostile frontiers to secure West Asian sea lanes.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Harappan Bead Making
masteryZone.sol: Explain the steps: sourcing raw stones (carnelian, jasper, steatite), heating to change color, chipping and grinding to shape, polishing to smooth, and drilling holes using hard chert drills.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Sluice-Gate Siphon Docking
masteryZone.sol: Explain how a sluice gate works: it is lowered to lock water in a basin when the external tide recedes, preventing ships from grounding on mud during low tides.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Craft Specialisation Suburbs
masteryZone.sol: Explain that some towns grew exclusively around specialized industrial crafts (like Chanhudaro) without needing administrative citadels or political elites, indicating a decentralized economic network.

sections.title: 3. Regional Enclaves, Defensive Citadels & Dryland Towns (Dholavira, Kalibangan, Banawali, Surkotada)
sections.content:
Harappan planning shows high flexibility, adapting to local dryland environments, water scarcity, and defense needs. Dholavira, Kalibangan, Banawali, and Surkotada display distinct regional differences.

Dholavira's Hydraulic & Stone Architecture
  • Three-Tier Layout: Dholavira in Gujarat's Kutch is divided into three parts: Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town.
  • Hydraulic Engineering: Utilized check dams and 16 massive stone-cut reservoirs to harvest rainwater.
  • Stone Masonry & Script: Relied heavily on dressed local limestone (not baked brick). It also yielded the famous 10-character Indus signboard.
Kalibangan, Banawali & Surkotada

Kalibangan (Rajasthan) is famous for its pre-Harappan ploughed agricultural field, wooden drainage pipes, and series of brick fire altars. Banawali (Haryana) represents a unique radial town layout rather than a grid pattern, and yielded a high-quality terracotta toy plow. Surkotada (Gujarat) features a fortified rubble stone citadel and has yielded debated skeletal horse remains in its upper layers.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Dholavirans build massive stone-cut water reservoirs?
masteryZone.sol: To store seasonal rainwater runoff in the arid region of Kutch where perennial freshwater rivers were absent and groundwater was brackish.

masteryZone.q: Why is the ploughed field at Kalibangan significant?
masteryZone.sol: It provides the earliest evidence of grid-pattern agricultural plowing in the subcontinent, showing that they grew two different crops simultaneously.

masteryZone.q: Why did Banawali develop a radial town layout?
masteryZone.sol: It represents a regional variation or planning deviation where streets radiated from the citadel, possibly due to local topographies or slower expansion.

masteryZone.q: How did Dholavira's hydraulic system collect water?
masteryZone.sol: By constructing stone dams across seasonal streams (Manhar and Mansar) and channeling the collected runoff into massive stone-cut reservoirs surrounding the citadel.

masteryZone.q: How did Kalibangan agriculturalists plow fields?
masteryZone.sol: By using wooden plows drawn by oxen, creating shallow crossed furrows to sow crops with different heights (like mustard and chickpea) together.

masteryZone.q: How did Surkotada's citadel protect its inhabitants?
masteryZone.sol: By constructing massive rubble stone fortifications with thick watchtowers and a heavily protected gateway, separating the citadel and residential sectors.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Dholavira's Water Conservation System
masteryZone.sol: An network of 16 stone-cut reservoirs capable of storing over 250,000 cubic meters of water. The system displays advanced understanding of slope, check dams, and sedimentation control, showing how Harappans adapted to arid conditions.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Kalibangan Ploughed Field
masteryZone.sol: Excavations revealed a grid pattern of furrows in pre-mature levels. The north-south furrows are spaced closely while east-west furrows are wider, which matches modern Rajasthani practices of planting mustard and gram together.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Surkotada Citadel and Fortifications
masteryZone.sol: A small, heavily fortified site built of stone rubble and mud brick. Features a central gateway with a ramp and guard rooms, demonstrating that even small peripheral outposts in Kutch had strong military defenses.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Dholavira's Three-Tier City Structure
masteryZone.sol: Explain that Dholavira is divided into a Citadel (ruling class), a Middle Town (bureaucrats and merchants), and a Lower Town (artisans), all enclosed by stone fortification walls, unlike the two-tier brick layout of eastern sites.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Harappan Fire Altars
masteryZone.sol: Explain the fire altars found at Kalibangan: clay-lined pits containing charcoal, ash, and a central clay pillar. They are interpreted as evidence of Vedic-like fire worship, though this remains debated.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: The Horse in Harappan Archaeology
masteryZone.sol: Explain the horse bone controversy: Surkotada reported horse teeth and bones in late levels, but many scholars identify them as wild ass (khur) or post-Harappan intrusions, as horses are not depicted on seals.

1. Weights were standardized, cubical blocks typically carved from chert.
2. The lower weight values followed a binary progression (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) up to ratio 1600.
3. The base unit weight equivalent to ratio 16 was approximately 13.63 grams.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, showing the highly precise, standardized commercial measurements.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the metallurgy of the Harappans:
1. The bronze 'Dancing Girl' sculpture of Mohenjo-daro is a hollow casting made using a single-piece mold.
2. Bronze casting was done using the cire perdue (lost-wax) technique.
3. Iron tools were manufactured at specialized industrial suburbs like Chanhudaro.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: The Dancing Girl is a solid bronze casting, not a hollow casting. Statement 3 is incorrect: Iron was entirely unknown to the Harappans (it was a Bronze Age culture).

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the steatite Priest-King bust from Mohenjo-daro, consider the following statements:
1. It depicts a bearded figure with a shaved upper lip wearing a trefoil-patterned shawl.
2. The eyes are inlaid with shell or stone, and the ears show circular drill holes.
3. Similar stone sculptures of Priest-Kings have been discovered in large quantities at Dholavira.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Priest-King bust is a rare, unique find; very few such high-quality stone statues have been discovered, and Dholavira has not yielded any similar bust.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan burials:
1. Extended burials in a north-south orientation with head to the north were the most common.
2. Joint burials containing two skeletons have been excavated at Lothal's cemetery.
3. Cemetery R-37 at Harappa features unique coffin burials where bodies were placed inside cedar wood containers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and illustrate the variations in Harappan mortuary practices.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to Harappan pottery, consider the following statements:
1. The pottery was predominantly wheel-made, painted in Red and Black style.
2. Common decorative motifs included geometric patterns, pipal leaves, and animal drawings like fish scales.
3. Glazed pottery was widely manufactured and exported to Egypt.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Glazed pottery was extremely rare in the Harappan civilization and was not exported to Egypt.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the seals of the Indus Civilisation:
1. Seals were primarily square or rectangular blocks made of soft steatite soapstone.
2. Most seals contained short inscriptions along with animal motifs like the unicorn, zebu bull, or elephant.
3. Seals served as amulets and security tags stamped on clay sealings for commercial shipments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and explain the material, iconography, and functions of Harappan seals.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the terracotta figurines of the Harappan Civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. Terracotta figurines were hand-modeled and baked in kilns, representing animals, toys, and human forms.
2. The 'Mother Goddess' figurines are characterized by elaborate fan-shaped headdresses.
3. Terracotta art was highly sophisticated, utilizing the same complex wax molds as bronze casting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Terracotta figurines were hand-modeled (often crudely compared to stone and metal) and did not use wax molds, which were reserved for bronze casting.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding fire altars in the Harappan Civilisation:
1. Brick-lined ritual pits identified as fire altars have been found at Kalibangan and Lothal.
2. Fire altars have also been excavated inside the Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro.
3. These altars often contain ash, charcoal, and clay cakes, suggesting fire worship or ritual sacrifices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: No fire altars have been found at Mohenjo-daro or Harappa.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Kalibangan, consider the following statements:
1. It featured a lower town that was fortified separately from the Citadel.
2. Pre-Harappan layers yielded furrow marks showing grid plowing for dual cropping.
3. Copper tools were manufactured here using ores sourced from the Khetri mines.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and illustrate Kalibangan's urban planning, agricultural technology, and metal resource links.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the decline of the Harappan Civilisation:
1. R.E.M. Wheeler proposed the Aryan invasion theory based on cemetery skeletons showing trauma.
2. Modern studies link the decline to the drying up of the Ghaggar-Hakra river system due to tectonic diversions.
3. Severe, repeated floods caused by shifts in the Indus river course devastated Mohenjo-daro multiple times.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements represent major theories proposed by archaeologists for the gradual collapse of Harappan urban centers.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Dholavira, consider the following statements:
1. Check dams were constructed across seasonal streams like the Manhar and Mansar to collect water.
2. The city was surrounded by massive stone rubble walls with rectangular bastions.
3. A unique stadium with spectator seating has been identified within the middle town.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and represent Dholavira's advanced civic architecture and recreational structures.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Banawali:
1. It is located in the Fatehabad district of Haryana.
2. Unlike other cities, the streets did not follow a grid iron pattern but rather a radial plan.
3. The drainage system at Banawali was the most advanced in the entire civilisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Banawali had a very degenerate or poor drainage system; soak jars placed in streets were used instead of structured brick sewers.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Surkotada, consider the following statements:
1. The site is divided into a citadel and a residential lower town, both enclosed by a common stone fortification.
2. A unique pot burial containing skeletal remains covered by a stone slab was excavated here.
3. Surkotada lies in the Hisar district of Haryana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Surkotada is located in the Kutch region of Gujarat, not in Haryana.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Harappa:
1. It was first visited and described by Charles Masson in 1826.
2. The site was extensively destroyed by railway contractors seeking brick ballast in the 19th century.
3. It is situated on the left bank of the Ravi River.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Harappa is situated on the right bank (or left bank historically, but wait, the modern left bank of the dry course of Ravi River) - actually, Ravi River left bank is correct. Wait, let's keep it simple: Charles Masson visited in 1826 and railway contractors destroyed it. Both are correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the Pashupati Seal from Mohenjo-daro, consider the following statements:
1. It depicts a three-faced seated deity wearing a horned headdress in a yogic posture.
2. The deity is surrounded by four wild animals: an elephant, a tiger, a rhinoceros, and a buffalo.
3. Two antelopes or deer are depicted sitting beneath the seat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and accurately describe the iconography of the famous Pashupati (Proto-Shiva) seal.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the socio-political organization of the Harappan Civilisation:
1. The existence of uniform weights, measures, and brick ratios suggests a strong central coordination.
2. Priests are widely believed to have ruled the cities, with the Great Bath serving as a temple.
3. There is no direct archaeological evidence of military rule, standing armies, or weapons of conquest.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: While the Priest-King bust exists, there is no direct evidence of a theocracy or temples in Harappan archaeology.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the Indus Valley drainage system, consider the following statements:
1. Main drains running along streets were covered with brick slabs or stone blocks.
2. Houses had brick-lined soak pits to collect solid waste before wastewater entered the street drains.
3. Drains were equipped with regular inspection chambers or manholes for cleaning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, illustrating the extraordinary public sanitation standards of the Indus Civilisation.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Mohenjo-daro:
1. It was discovered by Rakhaldas Bannerjee in 1922.
2. The literal meaning of Mohenjo-daro in Sindhi is 'Mound of the Dead'.
3. It is situated on the banks of the Ghaggar River.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Mohenjo-daro is situated on the right bank of the Indus River.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the agricultural practices of the Harappans, consider the following statements:
1. The main crops cultivated were wheat, barley, peas, sesame, and mustard.
2. Rice grains were found in large quantities across all northern metropolises like Harappa.
3. Agriculture relied on monsoonal floods depositing silt rather than extensive canal networks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Rice remains are extremely rare and only reported from western sites like Lothal and Rangpur; northern metropolises relied on wheat and barley.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the animal domestication by Harappans:
1. Humped zebu bulls, sheep, goats, and domestic water buffaloes were commonly depicted and kept.
2. The lion was the most common animal represented on Harappan seals.
3. Elephants and rhinoceroses were known to the Harappans and depicted on seals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: The lion is completely absent from Harappan seals (though tigers are depicted).

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the stone sculpture of the Priest-King, consider the following statements:
1. It is made of soft steatite and depicts a bearded figure with a headband.
2. The figure is draped in a shawl decorated with a trefoil motif.
3. The sculpture was excavated at the site of Harappa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Priest-King bust was excavated at Mohenjo-daro, not Harappa.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Dholavira:
1. The fortifications and major public structures utilize local stone masonry instead of brick.
2. A large stadium or open ceremonial ground was found between the Citadel and Middle Town.
3. It is situated on the island of Khadir Bet in Gujarat's Kutch region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and represent Dholavira's geographical and architectural features.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the ploughed field of Kalibangan, consider the following statements:
1. It features two sets of furrows crossing at right angles, indicating dual cropping.
2. It belongs to the pre-Harappan or early Harappan phase of the site.
3. The field was irrigated by a system of brick-lined canals originating from the Sutlej.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: No canals were found at Kalibangan; agricultural irrigation was rain-fed or relied on inundations.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the trade connections of Harappans:
1. Mesopotamian records mention trade with 'Meluhha', widely identified as the Indus region.
2. Standardized Harappan seals have been found at Mesopotamian sites like Kish and Ur.
3. Dilmun (Bahrain) and Magan (Oman) acted as intermediate trading stations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, outlining the network of overseas maritime trade.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Chanhudaro, consider the following statements:
1. It is located in the Sindh province of Pakistan, south of Mohenjo-daro.
2. It was a dedicated industrial craft town without any administrative fortifications.
3. Metal-working, shell-carving, and bead-making were the primary economic activities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct. Chanhudaro was a craft suburb without military fortifications.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the bronze Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-daro:
1. It is a solid bronze figurine depicting a young woman in a dancing pose.
2. The figure wears a necklace and has her left arm covered with bangles.
3. It is currently preserved in the National Museum, New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing the characteristics and preservation of the Dancing Girl.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the town planning differences in the Kutch region, consider the following statements:
1. Dholavira utilized stone masonry extensively due to local stone availability.
2. Surkotada had a fortified citadel and lower town with a gateway built of rubble stone.
3. Both sites completely lacked any defensive fortification walls.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Both Dholavira and Surkotada were heavily fortified with massive stone walls.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Banawali:
1. It contains a fortified citadel that is separated from the lower town by a mud-brick wall.
2. The drainage system was very poor, utilizing soak jars placed at street corners.
3. It yielded a well-preserved terracotta model of a plow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct. Banawali represents a deviation from the standard grid planning and had poor drainage.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the religious practices of Harappans, consider the following statements:
1. Worship of Mother Goddess is inferred from terracotta female figurines.
2. Worship of Proto-Shiva is suggested by the Pashupati seal.
3. Large, monumental temples with assembly halls were built to house deities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: No temples or monumental religious buildings have been found in Harappan archaeology.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan weights:
1. Weights were predominantly cubical and made of chert.
2. The binary system was used for lower weights (up to ratio 64) and decimal for higher weights.
3. The weights are completely non-standardized and show large variations from site to site.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Harappan weights were highly standardized across all regions, showing a centralized administration.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to Harappan bead manufacturing, consider the following statements:
1. Bead-making factories have been identified at Lothal and Chanhudaro.
2. Carnelian beads were manufactured by heating raw stone to obtain a red color.
3. Dressed stone drills of hard chert were used to drill holes through the beads.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct and describe the materials and steps in Harappan bead manufacture.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the script of the Indus Valley Civilisation:
1. The script is pictographic and remains undeciphered.
2. The writing direction was boustrophedon (right to left on one line, left to right on the next).
3. It was exclusively written on large stone tablets and signboards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: The script was written on seals, copper tablets, pottery, and ivory rods, as well as the Dholavira signboard.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Rakhigarhi, consider the following statements:
1. It is the largest Harappan site by area, covering over 350 hectares.
2. It has yielded a large cemetery showing diverse burial patterns.
3. It is located in the Hisar district of Haryana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct and define Rakhigarhi's size, burial site, and geographical location.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Kalibangan:
1. It contains a fortified citadel and a fortified lower town.
2. A series of fire altars were found built on brick platforms.
3. It yielded a unique terracotta ploughed field model.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: The ploughed field at Kalibangan is a real agricultural field in the soil, not a terracotta model (the toy plow was found at Banawali).

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Lothal, consider the following statements:
1. It was an important administrative capital of the northern region.
2. It featured a dockyard connected to the Bhogavo River.
3. Double burials of male-female pairs were found here.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: Lothal was a southern port city and trade enclave, not a northern administrative capital (which was Harappa).

mockTestQuestions.q:
Match the unique architectural or civic features of the Harappan towns with their respective sites:
1. Dholavira - Dressed stone masonry & reservoirs
2. Kalibangan - Pre-Harappan ploughed field
3. Banawali - Radial streets & toy plow
4. Lothal - Baked-brick tidal dockyard
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All four pairs are correct matches of the unique features associated with these towns.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the site of Rakhigarhi:
1. It is the largest geographical site of the Indus Valley Civilisation, covering over 350-500 hectares.
2. Recent DNA studies of its skeletal remains show genetic continuity without massive migrations from the West.
3. It is situated along the dry channel of the Drishadvati River in Haryana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, outlining the geographic, riverine, and genetic research significance of Rakhigarhi.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Chanhudaro?
1. It was a dedicated craft suburb specializing in bead-making, seal-cutting, and shell-working.
2. Unlike other major Harappan towns, it completely lacks a fortified citadel structure.
Select the correct answer:
mockTestQuestions.sol: Chanhudaro was a pure craft town that completely lacked an administrative citadel fortification.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Surkotada in Gujarat, consider the following statements:
1. It featured a fortified citadel and residential lower town constructed using local stone rubble.
2. Excavations in its upper layers reported the skeletal remains of a horse, which remains a subject of debate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct, describing Surkotada's stone-walled fort and horse bone findings.

mockTestQuestions.q: The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro was made watertight by applying a layer of bitumen. Bitumen is a:
opts: Natural tar applied over a brick-and-gypsum mortar backing
Glazed chemical paste imported from Egypt
Powdered limestone mixed with tree sap
Varnish made from boiled cedar wood resin
mockTestQuestions.sol: Natural bitumen (tar) was mined and applied over brickwork to prevent leakage.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan burials:
1. Cemetery R-37 at Harappa contains burials where bodies were placed in cedar wooden coffins.
2. Lothal has yielded joint burials containing skeletons of a male and a female.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both statements represent verified archaeological discoveries in Harappan mortuary practices.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to Harappan bead-making technology, consider the following statements:
1. Beads were made from carnelian, jasper, crystal, and steatite.
2. Carnelian beads were heated over fire to obtain their characteristic red color.
3. Dressed chert or bronze drills were used to perforate the beads.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, explaining the raw materials, heating, and drilling steps in bead production.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the geographical boundaries of the Harappan Civilisation:
1. Sutkagendor on the Dasht River marked the westernmost boundary.
2. Manda on the Chenab River marked the northernmost limit.
3. Daimabad on the Pravara River marked the southernmost limit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three boundary sites are correctly matched to their corresponding rivers and cardinal limits.

mockTestQuestions.q: The Harappan weight system relied on chert blocks following a binary system for lower weights. What was the base unit?
mockTestQuestions.sol: The base unit weight of the binary system was 13.63 grams.

mockTestQuestions.q: The Dancing Girl bronze figurine represents advanced metal casting. Which technique was used to manufacture it?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Lost-wax casting was the standard method for casting bronze art.
